rendered: According to the document, NMC 811[1] showed only minimal lithium leaching into water at the longest exposure point. The text gives the figure as about ~3 wt%[2] after one week[3]. The source sentence reads: leaching (~3 wt%) after one week[4]. The chart in Fig. 4[5] plots the wt% of lithium leached for each composition over exposure time, and its highest curve, the high-nickel composition, sits at roughly the same level at that final time point, so the approximate value quoted from the text is the best reading. The figure itself gives no exact value.[6]

source.caption: Fig. 4. a) wt% of lithium leached from NMC into water for four different NMC compositions as measured by ICP-MS. b) Long-term cycle life comparison for single- layer full pouch cells assembled with graphite anodes and either aqueous-processed or NMP-processed NMC 811 cathodes. Total cathode loadings were between 11.3 and 11.6 mg/cm^2. Cells were charged and discharged at C/3. Error bars represent the standard deviation of multiple cells (averaged every 25 cycles). The small break in the data is due to a power outage that caused the cells to cycle without the data being recorded when the power returned. Adapted from Reference 21 with permission from Elsevier.
